_doc: PINNED OLLAMA RELEASE — the only Ollama artifact the CI lanes may install.
WHY. Until 2026-08-16 every heartbeat tick ran `curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh`:
a remote script fetched over the network and handed straight to a shell, on a 15-minute cron,
on a job holding contents:write and pull-requests:write. Whatever that URL served at that
instant executed with the runner's token in the environment. That is influence entering
through an undeclared, unmetered channel — manifesto §13, noninterference / entropy
quarantine — and it was the sharpest instance in the egress inventory.
SHAPE. This file is an ace PackageEntry (src/Core.TypeScript/ace/ace-cli.ts) plus the
artifact locator ace does not model yet. A content-addressed install IS a hash-pinned
install, so the pin is written in the shape ace will eventually consume rather than in an
ad-hoc format someone would later have to unwind. `entry` is verbatim-shaped for ace;
`artifact` is the part ace has no field for today. NOTHING IN ACE READS THIS FILE YET —
see `aceGaps`. Claiming otherwise would be the vacuous-check shape.
REFRESH (the maintenance path):
1. bun src/Core.TypeScript/ace/refresh-ollama-pin.ts [--tag vX.Y.Z]  # rewrites entry + artifact
2. commit on a branch, push, open a PR
3. verify-ollama-pin.yml runs ON THAT PR automatically and proves the pin on a real
ubuntu-24.04 runner — install, serve, pull, complete, plus the REFUSAL path
4. merge only after it is green
The refresher cross-checks the digest against TWO independent sources (the release's own
sha256sum.txt and GitHub's API-reported asset digest) and refuses to write if they
disagree. Hashing the file you just downloaded and pinning that is a check that cannot fail.
FAILURE MODE WHEN UPSTREAM MOVES: nothing happens. The URL is version-addressed, so a new
upstream release does not touch us — the pin goes stale, it does not break. It fails only if
the tagged asset is deleted or its bytes change, and then the install step goes RED and the
tick continues WITHOUT a model. It never falls back to the unpinned installer.
aceGaps: ace-cli.ts install() performs NO download and NO filesystem write — it is a pure Z-set delta over a 4-row hardcoded STUB_REGISTRY whose contentAddresses are literals ('sha256:abc123'). Verified by reading the source 2026-08-16, and its own header says so.

ace.ts DOES have a real fetch + package_hash-verified install with lock-pin refusal — but it fetches `.text()`, i.e. JSON package manifests. It has no binary-artifact path, so a 1.4GB .tar.zst is out of scope for it today.
PackageEntry has no artifact locator (url/asset/platform) and no archive-extraction concept. `artifact` above is exactly the field set ace would need to own this row.

PackageEntry.packageManager is the union "ace"|"helm"|"npm"|"cargo"|"nix"; there is no member for a vendor release binary. "ace" is recorded here as the least-wrong value, not as a claim that ace manages it.

graphMerkleRoot() is a 32-bit non-cryptographic string hash, so ace's graph root is not today an integrity primitive. The integrity here rests on the SHA-256 in `entry.contentAddress`, checked by src/Core.TypeScript/ace/pinned-artifact.ts — not on ace.

`artifact.verify` (binary + versionArgs) is a post-install proof that the thing on PATH came out of the archive we verified. ace has no equivalent: its `verify` compares a recorded contentAddress against the registry, which cannot notice that an older build is shadowing the installed one.
